explanation: Brewers begin by polishing away the outer layers of each grain. A mould called koji then turns the starch into sugar, which yeast ferments, a process closer to brewing beer than making wine.

claims.text: Sake is not brewed from barley, wheat or millet.
For sake, rice grains are polished to remove their outer layers.
In sake brewing, koji mould (Aspergillus oryzae) converts rice starch into sugar, which yeast ferments into alcohol.
Because sake is made by converting starch to sugar and then fermenting it, its production resembles beer brewing more than winemaking.
